content: This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to understand how to use this information. This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Ocuflox Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat bacterial eye infections. Ofloxacin belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial eye infections and will not work for other types of eye infections. How to Use: 1. Before applying the eye drops, wash your hands thoroughly. 2. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. 3. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. 4. Hold the dropper directly above the eye and place one drop into the affected eye. 5. Look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. 6. Use one finger to apply gentle pressure to the inner corner of the eye (near the nose) to prevent the medication from draining out. 7. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes after application. 8. Do not rinse the dropper. 9. If you are using other eye medications (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5 minutes before applying the next medication. 10. Use this medication regularly to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Temporary stinging or burning of the eyes may occur for 1 to 2 minutes after application. Other possible side effects include temporary blurred vision, eye discomfort, itching, redness, dryness, tearing, a sensation of something in the eye, or sensitivity to light. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before using ofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other quinolones (such as ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride) that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Avoid driving or operating machinery until your vision is clear. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Consult your doctor for more details. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: This medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature. Discard the solution if it changes color, becomes cloudy, or develops particles. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal instructions. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized guidance.
